Exercise 3.2 · Week 3

Shape Family

Python in Thonny Work in pairs

Goal: build a family of shape classes. They all inherit from Shape, but each one overrides draw() to make its own picture.

  1. Open starter.py in Thonny. Read Shape and Square first.
  2. Finish the TODOs:
    • Triangle.draw - 3 sides, left(120).
    • Star.draw - 5 sides, right(144).
    • Polygon.__init__ - call super().__init__(x, y, size, color).
  3. Press Run. You should see a 4 x 3 grid of squares, triangles, stars and hexagons in 7 colors (each kind also has its own shape, so you can tell them apart without color).

Extra: add a Flower(Shape) class whose draw repeats a small circle 6 times while turning 60 degrees. Add it to make_pattern.

Starter code

Open starter.py in Thonny, or copy the code below into a new file and save it as starter.py.

# Shape Family - YOUR version
# Every shape IS A Shape: it shares x, y, size, color and the start() method.
# Each child overrides draw() - so the same call, shape.draw(t), makes a
# different picture for every class (polymorphism).
# Finish the TODOs, then press Run and see if it does what the README says.

import turtle

PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7"]


class Shape:
    """Parent class. A plain Shape is drawn as a dot."""

    def __init__(self, x, y, size, color):
        self.x = x
        self.y = y
        self.size = size
        self.color = color

    def start(self, t):
        """Move the turtle to this shape's corner, ready to draw."""
        t.penup()
        t.goto(self.x, self.y)
        t.setheading(0)
        t.pendown()
        t.color("black", self.color)

    def draw(self, t):
        self.start(t)
        t.dot(self.size, self.color)


class Square(Shape):
    """(Already done - use it as an example!)"""

    def draw(self, t):
        self.start(t)
        t.begin_fill()
        for _ in range(4):
            t.forward(self.size)
            t.left(90)
        t.end_fill()


class Triangle(Shape):
    # TODO 1: override draw(self, t): like Square, but 3 sides and left(120)
    pass


class Star(Shape):
    # TODO 2: override draw(self, t): 5 sides of self.size, turning right(144)
    pass


class Polygon(Shape):
    """A shape with any number of sides. It needs one extra attribute."""

    def __init__(self, x, y, size, color, sides):
        # TODO 3: call super().__init__(x, y, size, color) first
        self.sides = sides

    def draw(self, t):
        self.start(t)
        t.begin_fill()
        for _ in range(self.sides):
            t.forward(self.size)
            t.left(360 / self.sides)
        t.end_fill()


def draw_all(shapes, t):
    """Draw every shape. We do not need to know which class each one is!"""
    for shape in shapes:
        shape.draw(t)


def make_pattern():
    """Build a 4 x 3 grid of shapes, cycling through classes and colors."""
    shapes = []
    index = 0
    for row in range(3):
        for col in range(4):
            x = -300 + col * 160
            y = 120 - row * 150
            color = PALETTE[index % len(PALETTE)]
            kind = index % 4
            if kind == 0:
                shapes.append(Square(x, y, 70, color))
            elif kind == 1:
                shapes.append(Triangle(x, y, 80, color))
            elif kind == 2:
                shapes.append(Star(x, y + 50, 90, color))
            else:
                shapes.append(Polygon(x, y, 40, color, 6))
            index = index + 1
    return shapes


if __name__ == "__main__":
    screen = turtle.Screen()
    screen.title("Shape Family")
    screen.tracer(0)
    pen = turtle.Turtle()
    pen.hideturtle()
    pen.pensize(2)
    draw_all(make_pattern(), pen)
    screen.update()
    turtle.done()

Stuck? Open a hint

Try on your own first. Hints open one at a time, from a small nudge to a bigger one. None of them gives the answer away.

Hint 1: Where to look

Read Square first. It is a finished example. Triangle and Star look almost the same, but with different sides and turns. Then look at Polygon.__init__. It saves sides but forgets something.

Hint 2: Try this

Copy the pattern from Square.draw: call self.start(t), fill, and repeat. Use range(...) for the number of sides. For Polygon, call super().__init__(...) so the parent saves x, y, size and color. Turtle uses left and right to turn.

Hint 3: Almost there

A shape draws like this: self.start(t), t.begin_fill(), for _ in range(____):, then t.forward(self.size) and t.left(____) or t.right(____), then t.end_fill(). Use the sides and turn from the README. In Polygon, write super().__init__(____, ____, ____, ____).
